short: Parliament passed a conservative religious act reinforcing traditional Catholic doctrine.
full:
On 28 June 1539, the Act of Six Articles received royal assent, signalling a severe conservative backlash against the growing evangelical movement in England. Championed forcefully by King Henry VIII himself, the legislation strongly reaffirmed traditional Catholic practices, officially mandating clerical celibacy, transubstantiation, and auricular confession, while prescribing death by burning for any public denial of these core tenets.

The act starkly demonstrated that while Henry had violently rejected papal political authority, he remained deeply orthodox and traditional in his personal theology. It forced radical reformers underground or into exile, caused the immediate resignation of reformist bishops like Hugh Latimer, and established the complex, uniquely Henrician hybrid of Catholicism without the Pope that characterized his later reign.
